8 (https://t.me/dlmehr/4912). Tempus’s ECG-PH software received FDA clearance to detect pulmonary-hypertension indicators from standard ECGs.
9. AI is on track to write nearly one in three medical SOAP notes.
10 (https://t.me/dlmehr/4914). The FDA authorized Aletta, the first standalone robotic device designed to draw blood without hands-on operator intervention.
11 (https://t.me/dlmehr/4915). MrBeast’s thumbnail team localizes one image by changing the police car according to the viewer’s language and country.
12 (https://t.me/dlmehr/4916). GPT-5.6 Sol pricing fell to $4 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.
13 (https://t.me/dlmehr/4917). A new Economist article reflects how AI consciousness has moved from a fringe topic into mainstream debate.
14 (https://t.me/dlmehr/4918). The Trump administration proposed a six-figure fee for most new H-1B visa applicants.
15 (https://t.me/dlmehr/4919). A Forrester survey found 55% of companies that cut workers citing AI now regret it, with many rehiring.
16 (https://t.me/dlmehr/4920). This post contains only a brief reaction with no substantive explanation.
17 (https://t.me/dlmehr/4921). Thomson Reuters built its own AI model on Alibaba’s Qwen to reduce reliance on Claude.
18 (https://t.me/dlmehr/4922). AgentSky launched a unified API for Claude Code, Codex, DeepSeek, Kimi, and other agents, highlighting a $150-versus-$2 task cost difference.
19 (https://t.me/dlmehr/4923). Apple may launch a new Mac mini before its September iPhone event.
20 (https://t.me/dlmehr/4924). Meta is preparing Hatch, a consumer agent potentially priced at $199.99 monthly and designed to work across services such as DoorDash and Outlook.

--Hermes (2/2)
